sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: UPR LOW WILL REMAIN QSTNRY NEAR JAMES BAY THIS PERIOD...MAINTAINING BROAD CYCLONIC FLOW OVER THE ERN TWO-THIRDS OF THE CONUS. SHORTWAVE IMPULSE NOW OVER SD SHOULD CONTINUE SE INTO THE LWR MO VLY THIS EVE...AND INTO THE MID MS/LWR OH VLY BY 12Z SUN...AS WEAKER DOWNSTREAM IMPULSES MOVE ESE FROM OK/E TX INTO THE LWR MS VLY/GULF CST STATES. ELSEWHERE...UPR RDG WILL PROGRESS SLOWLY E ACROSS THE GRT BASIN/INTERMOUNTAIN WEST...WHILE A TROUGH/LOW OVER THE NE PACIFIC MOVES NNE TO VANCOUVER ISLAND. AT THE SFC...WEAK COLD FRONT ASSOCIATED WITH SD IMPULSE WILL MOVE S ACROSS THE CNTRL PLNS TO A TX PANHANDLE-SE NEB LINE BY THIS EVE...WHERE IT WILL INTERSECT A WARM/STNRY FRONT EXTENDING ESE ALONG THE RED RVR. ANOTHER DIFFUSE BOUNDARY...COMPLICATED BY MCS OUTFLOW...WILL REMAIN QSTNRY FROM E TX EWD INTO CNTRL AL/GA. FROM THERE THE BOUNDARY WILL CONTINUE NEWD AS A COLD FRONT OFF THE NC CST.

sections.title: CNTRL/SRN PLNS SE INTO ARKLATEX/LWR MS VLY THROUGH TNGT
sections.text: AFOREMENTIONED WARM FRONT...AND OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES FROM OVERNIGHT CONVECTIVE CLUSTERS...SHOULD SERVE TO FOCUS LOW LVL CONVERGENCE/DIURNALLY ENHANCED TSTM DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE PERIOD FROM PARTS OF TX AND OK ESE INTO THE LWR MS VLY. PATTERN/TIMING OF CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT WILL...HOWEVER...BE COMPLICATED BY THE DIFFUSE/FRAGMENTED NATURE OF THE BOUNDARIES...BY CONSIDERABLE CLOUD COVER...AND BY IMPULSES IN WNWLY MID/UPR LVL FLOW. A FORWARD-PROPAGATING CONVECTIVE SYSTEM MAY EVENTUALLY ARISE FROM ONGOING...LOOSELY ORGANIZED CLUSTER OF SLIGHTLY ELEVATED STORMS NOW OVER SE OK/SRN AR. GIVEN INSTABILITY/PW DEPICTED IN AREA OBSERVED AND FCST SOUNDINGS...SUCH A SYSTEM COULD CONTAIN SMALL- SCALE BOW STRUCTURES WITH DMGG WIND/SVR HAIL. A SIMILAR FORWARD-PROPAGATING SYSTEM MAY ARISE NEAR COLD FRONT/WARM FRONT INTERSECTION IN THE TX PANHANDLE REGION/SW KS...AND MOVE SE INTO WRN OK/N TX...WHERE WEAK UPSLOPE FLOW EXISTS. STRENGTHENING WIND FIELDS /40+ KT NNW DEEP SHEAR/ AND ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH GRAZING INFLUENCE OF SD UPR IMPULSE WILL YIELD AN ENVIRONMENT SUPPORTIVE OF SUSTAINED STORMS AND SUPERCELLS... ESPECIALLY OVER WRN HALF OF SLIGHT RISK AREA. SOME OF THE ACTIVITY IN THE LATTER AREA MAY IN

sections.title: CAROLINAS/MID-ATLANTIC STATES
sections.text: STRONG SFC HEATING WILL OCCUR TODAY ALONG DIFFUSE COLD FRONT AND LEE TROUGH OVER THE ERN CAROLINAS/SE VA...BOOSTING SBCAPE TO AOA 1500 J/KG. AT THE SAME TIME...UPR DIVERGENCE WILL INCREASE AS JET ENTRANCE REGION EVOLVES ON ERN FLANK OF BROAD UPR LVL TROUGH. ALTHOUGH WSWLY DEEP SHEAR WILL REMAIN FAIRLY MODEST /30-35 KTS/...OVERALL SETUP MAY YIELD SHORT LINES/CLUSTERS OF MULTICELL STORMS WITH LOCALLY DMGG WIND THROUGH EARLY EVE.

sections.title: INTERIOR WRN/CNTRL ORE THIS AFTN/EVE
sections.text: HEIGHT FALLS/INCREASING MID/UPR LVL FLOW WILL BRUSH WRN ORE IN ASSOCIATION WITH OFFSHORE TROUGH. DIFFERENTIAL HEATING OF THE HIGHER TERRAIN SHOULD RESULT ISOLD TO WDLY SCTD TSTMS BY MID-LATE AFTN IN MODESTLY MOIST/DEEPLY MIXED ENVIRONMENT. THE STORMS MAY YIELD ISOLD DMGG WIND GUSTS THROUGH EARLY TNGT. ..CORFIDI/HURLBUT.. 08/18/2012

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: LONGWAVE TROUGH --ANCHORED BY UPPER LOW OVER JAMES BAY-- WILL BE MAINTAINED E OF THE ROCKIES THROUGH THE D1 PERIOD. SEVERAL VORTICITY MAXIMA WILL MOVE THROUGH THE CYCLONIC...BROAD-SCALE PATTERN...THE MOST NOTABLE OF WHICH WILL TRANSLATE FROM THE NRN PLAINS INTO THE OZARKS AND MID MS VALLEY. ELSEWHERE...A SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL MOVE ONTO THE PACIFIC NW/NRN CA COAST LATER TODAY INTO TONIGHT. IN THE LOW LEVELS...WRN EXTENSION OF SYNOPTIC FRONT OVER THE CNTRL/SRN PLAINS HAS BEEN MODULATED BY ONGOING TSTM COMPLEXES. AS OF 16Z...GREATEST THETA GRADIENT EXTENDED FROM OK/TX PNHDLS SEWD TO ALONG THE RED RIVER VALLEY. EXPECT THIS SEGMENT OF FRONT TO EVENTUALLY BE DISPLACED SWD OWING TO GROWING CONVECTIVE COLD POOLS AND INCREASING SURFACE PRESSURE RISES OVER THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS WITH PASSAGE OF ABOVE-MENTIONED VORTICITY MAXIMUM TO THE E/SE. MEANWHILE...PORTION OF FRONT OVER THE GULF COAST STATES MAY LIFT SLIGHTLY NWD IN RESPONSE TO DEVELOPING WEAK SURFACE WAVE OVER THE LOWER MS VALLEY...WHILE ERN SEGMENT OF BOUNDARY REMAINS QUASI-STATIONARY OVER THE CAROLINAS. ...SRN HIGH PLAINS INTO LOWER MS VALLEY THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT... 12Z REGIONAL SOUNDINGS AND CURRENT SURFACE OBSERVATIONS INDICAT

sections.title: CAROLINAS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING
sections.text: 12Z CHS SOUNDING REVEALED THE POTENTIAL FOR MODERATE-STRONG INSTABILITY /I.E. SBCAPE OF 2000-3000 J PER KG/ THIS AFTERNOON OWING TO A VERY MOIST ENVIRONMENT WITH A PW VALUE OF AROUND TWO INCHES. WHILE LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL REMAIN SOMEWHAT NEBULOUS...WEAK CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT OVER UPSTATE SC AS OF 16Z MAY BE ASSOCIATED WITH A WEAK VORTICITY MAXIMUM WHICH WILL TRACK ACROSS THE PIEDMONT TOWARD THE COASTAL PLAIN. FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH THIS FEATURE IN COMBINATION WITH PRESENCE OF SYNOPTIC FRONT AND DEVELOPING SEA BREEZE FRONT WILL FOSTER AN INCREASE IN STORMS THIS AFTERNOON...A FEW OF WHICH WILL BE CAPABLE OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND GUSTS.

sections.title: PACIFIC NW
sections.text: FORCING FOR ASCENT/DCVA WILL INCREASE TODAY IN ADVANCE OF SHORTWAVE TROUGH APPROACHING THE COAST. 12Z SALEM AND MEDFORD SOUNDINGS SHOWED STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AND PW VALUES OF 0.9-1.4 INCHES WHICH WILL SUPPORT AT LEAST MODEST AFTERNOON INSTABILITY AND THE POTENTIAL FOR ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS CAPABLE OF HAIL AND LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. ..MEAD/SMITH.. 08/18/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE RISK FOR AT LEAST LOCALIZED STRONG SURFACE GUSTS NEAR STORMS MAY NOT BE NEGLIGIBLE...BUT SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL STILL SEEMS LOW ENOUGH THAT A WATCH IS NOT ANTICIPATED IN THE NEAR TERM. TRENDS WILL...HOWEVER...CONTINUE TO BE CLOSELY MONITORED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE SMALL CLUSTER OF THUNDERSTORMS WHICH HAS SPREAD ACROSS THE GARDEN CITY AND DODGE CITY AREAS WITHIN THE LAST COUPLE OF HOURS HAS BEEN FLUCTUATING IN INTENSITY...BUT GENERALLY REMAINS FAIRLY VIGOROUS AS IT APPROACHES THE OKLAHOMA/KANSAS BORDER TO THE NORTHWEST OF ALVA OK. THIS ACTIVITY IS OCCURRING IN THE WAKE OF SEVERAL DOWNSTREAM CONVECTIVE CLUSTERS...WITHIN WEAK TO MODERATE NORTHWEST FLOW ACROSS THE SOUTHERN PLAINS. OUTFLOW ASSOCIATED WITH THESE CLUSTERS HAS REINFORCED THE RELATIVELY COOL/STABLE BOUNDARY LAYER NEAR/NORTHEAST OF A REMNANT STALLED SURFACE FRONT ACROSS THE RED RIVER VALLEY REGION. THIS SEEMS TO LIMIT DOWNBURST POTENTIAL...PARTICULARLY GIVEN THE WEAKNESS OF THE AMBIENT LOW- LEVEL FLOW FIELDS. HOWEVER...DEVELOPING SURFACE PRESSURE PERTURBATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH THE CONVECTION HAVE BEEN SIGNIFICANT ENOUGH TO CONTRIBUTE TO STRONG SURFACE GUSTS ACROSS SOUTHWEST KANSAS...WHERE ONE SIGNIFICANT FALL/RISE COUPLET WAS EVIDENT NEAR/SOUTHEAST OF DODGE CITY AT 14Z. GIVEN THE EXTENT OF THE DOWNSTREAM CONVECTION...WHICH CONTINUES TO INCREASE IN COVERAGE...THE LONGEVITY OF THIS FEATURE...AND THE EXTENT OF THE SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL IN THE SHORT TERM REMAINS UNCLEAR...BUT STILL SEEMS LOW AT THE PRESENT TIME.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL STILL APPEARS RELATIVELY LOW IN THE NEAR TERM...BUT MAY SLOWLY INCREASE THROUGH THE EARLY AFTERNOON HOURS ACROSS PARTS OF NORTHEASTERN LOUISIANA INTO CENTRAL MISSISSIPPI. IT IS NOT CERTAIN THAT A WW WILL BE NEEDED...BUT TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THUNDERSTORMS HAVE RECENTLY FORMED AND INTENSIFIED WITHIN A NORTH-SOUTH BAND...ROUGHLY ALONG A LINE FROM EAST OF EL DORADO AR SOUTHWARD INTO AREAS EAST OF NATCHITOCHES LA. THIS IS GENERALLY WELL SOUTH OF THE STRONGER WESTERLIES...WITHIN CONVECTIVE LAYER MEAN FLOW THAT APPEARS GENERALLY ON THE ORDER OF 10-15 KTS OR LESS. THERMODYNAMIC PROFILES ARE CHARACTERIZED BY MODEST LAPSE RATES...AT BEST...BUT HIGH MOISTURE CONTENT /UP TO AROUND 2 INCHES/ IS CONTRIBUTING TO SIZABLE CAPE SUPPORTIVE OF INTENSE UPDRAFTS WITH HEAVY RAIN AND HAIL. GIVEN THE RELATIVELY WARM PROFILES...SEVERE HAIL REACHING THE SURFACE APPEARS LOW. HOWEVER ...HEAVY PRECIPITATION LOADING COULD CONTRIBUTE TO DOWNBURSTS WITH LOCALIZED STRONG SURFACE GUSTS. THROUGH 17-19Z...THIS POTENTIAL APPEARS HIGHEST WHERE LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE WILL BE ENHANCED NEAR THE INTERSECTION OF THE EASTWARD ADVANCING CONVECTIVE LINE AND A LINGERING EAST-WEST FRONTAL ZONE...EAST OF MONROE LA INTO THE JACKSON MS AREA.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AT LEAST SCATTERED STRONG/SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED AS EARLY AS 20-21Z. TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR THE POSSIBILITY OF A SEVERE WEATHER WATCH.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: BENEATH A MID-LEVEL ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY STEEP LAPSE RATES AND MODEST WEST NORTHWESTERLY FLOW...SURFACE HEATING OF A MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER IS CONTRIBUTING TO STEEPENING LOW-LEVEL LAPSE AND MODERATELY LARGE MIXED LAYER CAPE NEAR A WEAK FRONTAL LOW EAST OF CHILDRESS TX. LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE APPEARS TO BE INCREASING ALONG THE FRONT EAST SOUTHEAST OF THE LOW THROUGH THE WICHITA FALLS AREA...WHERE STRENGTHENING MID/UPPER FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL MOTION ASSOCIATED WITH THE DIGGING UPSTREAM SHORT WAVE TROUGH WILL CONTINUE TO WEAKEN INHIBITION DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS. THE HIGH RESOLUTION RAPID REFRESH SUGGESTS INITIATION OF STORMS IS POSSIBLE AS EARLY AS 20-21Z...AS THE SURFACE TEMPERATURES WARM THROUGH THE LOWER/MID 90S. LOW-LEVEL FLOW FIELDS ARE FAIRLY WEAK...BUT VEERING WITH HEIGHT BENEATH STRENGTHENING MID-LEVEL FLOW IS EXPECTED TO YIELD SUFFICIENT VERTICAL SHEAR FOR SUPERCELLS. LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE INITIALLY. AN ISOLATED/BRIEF TORNADO MAY NOT BE OUT OF THE QUESTION...BUT...GIVEN THE RATHER WARM AND DEEPLY MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER...WITH SIZABLE TEMPERATURE-DEW POINT SPREADS... THE RISK FOR STRONG DAMAGING WIND GUSTS APPEARS MOST PROMINENT... ASSOCIATED WITH DOWNBURSTS AND STRONG SURFACE COLD POOL DEVELOPMENT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WHILE ISOLATED SVR STORMS REMAIN POSSIBLE ACROSS THE WW AREA...THE OVERALL THREAT IS RATHER MARGINAL.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A BAND OF LOOSELY ORGANIZED CONVECTIVE CLUSTERS FROM FLOYD COUNTY TO BAYLOR COUNTY TX IS BEING UNDERCUT BY ITS ASSOCIATED COLD POOL WHILE LYING SOUTH OF ANY APPRECIABLE MID-LEVEL FLOW -- I.E. PROFILER DATA DEPICTING GENERALLY LESS THAN 20 KT OF FLOW AOB 5 KM AGL. AN ISOLATED SVR WIND GUST CANNOT BE RULED OUT WITH INCIPIENT CONVECTION OVER THE SRN FLANK OF THE SWD-EXPANDING COLD POOL AMIDST A RELATIVELY DEEP BOUNDARY LAYER CHARACTERIZED BY SFC TEMPS IN THE LOWER 90S AND DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 50S. HOWEVER...SUCH THREAT SHOULD BE SHORT IN DURATION...AND THE SVR THREAT SHOULD QUICKLY DIMINISH FOLLOWING THE PASSAGE OF THIS BAND. MULTICELL CLUSTERS OVER THE ERN EXTENT OF THE WW AREA MAY ALSO POSE A THREAT FOR ISOLATED MARGINALLY SVR WIND GUSTS AND SMALL HAIL...THOUGH MARGINAL DEEP SHEAR AND MORE ABUNDANT CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING SHOULD KEEP ANY SVR THREAT BRIEF/ISOLATED. ..COHEN.. 08/18/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SVR THREAT CONTINUES DECREASING ACROSS REMAINING VALID PARTS OF WW584...WHICH SHOULD BE ALLOWED TO EXPIRE BY THE SCHEDULED EXPIRATION TIME OF 02Z. ADDITIONAL WW ISSUANCE IS NOT NEEDED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CAPPI DATA AT 9 KM INDICATE AN OVERALL WEAKENING TREND OF ONGOING CONVECTION ACROSS THE ERN TWO-THIRDS OF THE WW AREA AS OUTFLOW CONTINUES UNDERCUTTING CONVECTION AMIDST ONLY MODEST DEEP SHEAR. NOCTURNAL STABILIZATION SHOULD REINFORCE THE WEAKENING TREND. WHILE INTENSE STORMS DEVELOPING S/SW OF THE AMARILLO AREA MAY TRANSITION SWD ACROSS WRN PARTS OF THE WW AREA...WITH ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT POSSIBLE FARTHER SOUTH ALONG A WWD-SURGING OUTFLOW BOUNDARY OVER THE TX SOUTH PLAINS...ALL OF THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD WEAKEN DURING THE NEXT HOUR OR TWO AS LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES BECOME INCREASINGLY POOR. ..COHEN.. 08/19/2012
